uncited: **Inputs:** A set of $V$ sparse input images (typically 3–9 views) with known camera poses; a grid-based NeRF representation (CP or VM decomposition) initialized with feature tensors.
**Outputs:** A trained radiance field model capable of novel view synthesis.
The scene is represented by a 3D feature tensor $\mathbf{T} \in \mathbb{R}^{I \times J \times K}$.
FourieRF operates on the factorized components of this tensor.
**CP Decomposition:** $\mathbf{T}$ is decomposed into a sum of rank-1 tensors.
The method applies frequency control to the 1D feature vectors $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
**VM Decomposition:** $\mathbf{T}$ is decomposed into a sum of outer products of a vector and a matrix (e.g., $\mathbf{v}_{r1} \circ \mathbf{M}_{r2,3}$).
**Initialization:** Initialize feature vectors and matrices in the spatial domain.
Compute the mask $\alpha(f_t)$ of length $d_f$ (dimension of FFT).
*   **2D Features ($\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_1 \times d_2}$):** (Used only in VM decomposition)
The mask is a circle centered at $c = (\lfloor d_1/2 \rfloor, \lfloor d_2/2 \rfloor)$ with radius $r = f_t \sqrt{\frac{\max(d_1, d_2)^2}{2}}$.
Coefficients outside the circle are set to 0.
**Network Forward Pass:** Use the smoothed features $\hat{\mathbf{v}}$ and $\hat{\mathbf{w}}$ to query the NeRF network for density and color.
**Loss Computation:** Compute the photometric loss (L2 or L1) between rendered and input images.
*   **Differentiability:** The threshold update $f_t$ must be applied at the start of the iteration, before any gradient is accumulated.
*   **Overfitting to Views:** In few-shot settings, models may overfit to directional information.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Inherits the memory complexity of the underlying grid decomposition (CP or VM).
*   **When to use:** Few-shot novel view synthesis (3–9 views) where training speed is critical and external data priors (depth, diffusion) are unavailable.
